facts.statement: Tambatitanis is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur classified as a titanosauriform, possibly a titanosaurian.
facts.quote: Tambatitanis (meaning "Tamba giant", after Tamba, the name given to the northwest of Kansai, Japan) is an extinct genus of titanosauriform, possibly titanosaurian, sauropod dinosaur

facts.statement: The genus Tambatitanis is known from a single species, Tambatitanis amicitiae, represented by a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: It is known from a single species, Tambatitanis amicitiae, known from a partial skeleton.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Tambatitanis was discovered in August 2006 by amateur paleontologists Shigeru Murakami and Kiyoshi Adachi.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of the Tambaitanis, MNHAH D-1029280 was initially discovered in August 2006, by Shigeru Murakami and Kiyoshi Adachi

facts.statement: The fossil was originally named 'Tamba-Ryu' before being formally published in 2014.
facts.quote: It was originally called 'Tamba-Ryu' before the publication in 2014.

facts.statement: Haruo Saegusa and Tadahiro Ikeda described Tambatitanis amicitiae as a new genus and species in 2014.
facts.quote: In 2014, Haruo Saegusa and Tadahiro Ikeda described Tambatitanis amicitiae as a new genus and species of titanosauriform sauropod based on these remains.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the lower Sasayama Group, which is believed to date to the early Albian.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MNHAH D-1029280, se ha encontrado en una capa del grupo Sasayama inferior, que se cree que data del Albiano temprano.

facts.statement: It took five years to excavate the fossil from a hard rock site covering an area of six by four meters.
facts.quote: Se necesitaron cinco años para desalojarlo en el sitio de la roca dura en un área de seis por cuatro metros.

facts.statement: The tail indicates a total length of between 10 and 15 meters.
facts.quote: La cola indica una longitud total de entre 10 y 15 metros.

facts.statement: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated the animal was around 14 meters long and weighed approximately 4 tons.
facts.quote: En 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimó que tenía alrededor de 14 metros de largo y su masa se estimó en unas 4 toneladas.

facts.statement: The chevron of the first tail vertebra is the longest of all known sauropods relative to body size.
facts.quote: El cheurón de la primera vértebra de la cola es el más largo de todos los saurópodos conocidos en comparación con el tamaño del cuerpo.

facts.statement: Tambatitanis lived during the Lower Cretaceous (lower Albian) in what is now Japan.
facts.quote: It is known from a single species, Tambatitanis amicitiae, known from a partial skeleton.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests Tambatitanis belonged to Euhelopodidae, but its specific placement within the group remains uncertain.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis from Saegusa and Ikeda (2014) suggests Tambatitanis was Euhelopodidae, but its specific placement is uncertain among this group due to polytomy shown in the matrix

facts.statement: An initial cladistic analysis placed Tambatitanis close to Qiaowanlong, Erketu, Euhelopus, Daxiatitan, Tangvayosaurus, and Phuwiangosaurus.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico inicial lo sitúa próximo a Qiaowanlong, Erketu, Euhelopus, Daxiatitan, Tangvayosaurus y Phuwiangosaurus.

facts.statement: Reviewers noted that initial results were preliminary and that the skull of Tambatitanis is more similar to that of Titanosauridae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, los revisores destacaron que estos resultados son preliminares y que el cráneo de Tambatitanis es más similar al de Titanosauridae.

facts.statement: Tambatitanis amicitiae lived during the mid-Cretaceous, between 112 and 109 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Tambatitanis amicitiae es la única especie conocida del género extinto Tambatitanis de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosauriforme que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, entre 112 a 109 millones de años, durante el Albiense, en lo que ahora es Asia.

facts.statement: The time range for Tambatitanis is the Albian, from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)
